description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): explains q_c = 3.4580993..., which k_versus_selected_operator_probe derived as the sign boundary of D_PN and which I there flagged as 'an unexplained structural constant'. That label is WITHDRAWN. Exactly, D_PN = -h(2 - delta)/4, so for q > 1 D_PN < 0 iff delta < 2, and the sextic in the D_PN numerator IS the equation delta = 2 rearranged (verified identical symbolically). The colour-weighted p-n interface is a weighted average (1/2 + delta/4) sigma + (1/2 - delta/4) sigma^-1 whose weights sum to 1; at q_c the sigma^-1 weight is exactly ZERO, so the interface degenerates to a pure sigma, and beyond q_c the weight is negative and it is no longer a convex combination. The earlier result that K(2H) leaves the positive sector exactly on 1 < q < q_c is then a tautology. At q_0, delta = 0.0013757 and the weights are 0.50034/0.49966 — within 0.07% of the symmetric average, three orders of magnitude below the boundary. What genuinely remains: the sextic is irreducible over Q so q_c is algebraic of degree exactly 6, and a grep of computations/, content/ and docs/ finds nothing in the corpus recording it. All exact (sympy). No fit; no B_AME; no physical claim.
caveats: RETRACTION: k_versus_selected_operator_probe called q_c 'an unexplained structural constant'. It is explained — the root of delta = 2, the convexity boundary of the colour-weighted p-n average. Only two narrower claims survive: q_c is algebraic of degree exactly 6, and the corpus does not record it.

This is a boundary of the PN_CONVENTION = 'bring_color_weighted' scheme specifically. Under 'strict_averaged' the offset is -h/2 with no delta, the weights are 1/2 and 1/2 at every q, and no such boundary exists. So q_c is a property of the colour weighting, not of the Hecke algebra.
No physical claim. Nothing here says q_c is meaningful beyond the algebra, and no physical quantity enters the computation.
